10.10: For indeed they say, “his letters are heavy and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech is of no value. ”
10.11: Let such a one think this: that as such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, we will also be in deed when we are present.
10.12: For we dare not reckon ourselves among, or compare ourselves to, those who praise themselves. But they do not understand that they measure themselves with themselves and compare themselves with themselves.
10.13: But we will not boast of things which are not measurable, but according to the measure of the rule which God has distributed to us; a measure to reach even to you.
10.14: For we do not stretch ourselves beyond measure, as though we had not reached you. For as far as you also we have come in the Gospel of Christ,
10.15: not boasting of things which are beyond measure ( that is, of others’ labors ). But we do hope, when your faith shall increase, to be magnified by you abundantly, according to our area,
10.16: and to preach the Gospel in those regions beyond you ( not to rejoice in another’s area which has already been prepared ).
10.17: But, “Let him who boasts, boast in the Lord”.
10.18: For the one who praises himself is not approved, but the one whom the Lord praises.

11.1: Would to God you could suffer a little of my foolishness, and indeed, suffer me.
11.2: For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy. For I have prepared you for one husband; to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
11.3: Yet I fear, however, that just as the serpent tricked Eve through his subtlety, so your minds may be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.
11.4: For if someone comes, preaching another Jesus whom we have not preached - or if you receive another spirit whom you have not received, or another gospel which you have not received - you might well tolerate him.
11.5: For I suppose that I am not inferior to the very chief Apostles.
11.6: And though I am unskilled in speaking, I am not so in knowledge. And among you we have made ourselves clearly understood in all things.
11.7: Have I committed an offense because I abased myself, that you might be exalted; and because I freely preached to you the Gospel of God?
11.8: I robbed other churches, taking wages from them to do you service.
11.9: And when I was present with you, and had need, I was not a hindrance to anyone. For that which I was lacking, the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied. And in all things, I have myself from being burdensome to you, and will keep doing so.
11.10: As the truth of Christ is in me, this rejoicing shall not be taken from me in the regions of Achaia.
11.11: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows.
11.12: But what I do I will do so that I may cut off the opportunity of those who desire the opportunity to be found like us in that of which they boast.
11.13: For such false apostles are deceitful workers and transform themselves into the Apostles of Christ.
11.14: And it is no wonder; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.
11.15: Therefore, it is no great thing for his ministers to transform themselves, as though they were the ministers of righteousness, whose end shall be according to their works.
11.16: I say again, let no one think that I am foolish, ( or even take me as a fool ) that I may also boast of myself a little.
11.17: What I speak, I do not speak according to the Lord but, as it were, foolishly, while we are boasting.
11.18: Seeing that many rejoice after the flesh, I will rejoice also.
11.19: For you endure fools gladly, because you are wise.
11.20: For you endure, even if someone enslaves you, if someone devours you, if someone takes from you, if someone exalts himself, if someone strikes you on the face.
11.21: Concerning dishonor I speak as though we were weak. But wherein anyone is bold ( I speak foolishly ) I am bold also.
11.22: They are Hebrews, so am I. They are Israelites, so am I. They are the seed of Abraham, so am I.
11.23: They are the ministers of Christ ( I speak as a fool ) I am more; In labors, more abundant; in stripes, above measure, in prison, more exceedingly; in death often.
11.24: Five times I have received forty stripes minus one from the Jews.
11.25: Three times I was beaten with rods. I was once stoned. I suffered shipwreck three times. Night and day, I have been on the deep sea.
11.26: While journeying I was often in perils from waters, in perils from robbers, in perils from my own nation, in perils among the Gentiles, in perils in the city, in perils in wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brothers,
11.27: in weariness and painfulness, in sleeplessness often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and in nakedness.
11.28: Besides outward things, I am daily - laden, and care for all the churches.
11.29: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is offended, and I do not burn?
11.30: If I must boast, I will boast of my infirmities.
11.31: The God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Who is blessed for evermore, knows that I do not lie.
11.32: In Damascus, the governor of the people under King Aretas, posted a guard over the city of the Damascenes, and would have caught me.
11.33: But at a window, I was let down in a basket, through the wall, and escaped his hands.

12.1: Doubtless, it is not profitable for me to boast. Yet, I will now come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
12.2: More than fourteen years ago I knew a man in Christ, ( whether he was in the body, I cannot tell, or out of the body, I cannot tell; God knows. ) who was taken up into the third heaven.
12.3: And I knew such a man ( whether in the body, or out of the body, I cannot tell; God knows ).
12.4: How that he was taken up into Paradise, and heard words which cannot be spoken, which are not possible for man to utter.
12.5: Of such a man I will boast. Of myself I will not boast, except that it be of my weakness.
12.6: For though I would desire to boast, I shall not be a fool; for I will say the truth. But I refrain, lest anyone should think me above that which he sees in me, or hears of me;
12.7: and lest I should be exalted out of measure through the abundance of revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, because I should not be exalted out of measure.
12.8: For this thing I implored the Lord three times, that it might depart from me.
12.9: And He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you. For My power is made perfect through weakness. ” Therefore, rather, I will very gladly boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
12.10: Therefore, I take pleasure in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in anguish for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
12.11: I have become a fool in boasting. You have compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you. For in nothing was I inferior to the very chief Apostles, though I am nothing.
12.12: Indeed, the signs of an Apostle were worked out among you with all patience; with signs and wonders and great works.
12.13: For in what have you been inferior to other churches, except that I myself have not been burdensome to you? Forgive me this wrong.
12.14: Behold, I am ready to come to you this third time. And yet I will not be burdensome to you. For I seek not what is yours, but you. For the children ought not to lay up for the fathers, but the fathers for the children.
12.15: And I will most gladly spend, and will be spent, for your souls; though, the more I love you, the less I am loved.
12.16: But let it be that I do not burden you. Yet for as much as I was crafty, I took you with guile.
12.17: Did I defraud you by any of those whom I sent to you?
12.18: I have urged Titus to go. And with him I have sent a brother. Did Titus defraud you of anything? Have we not walked in the selfsame spirit, in the same steps?
12.19: Again, do you think that we defend ourselves to you? We speak before God, in Christ. But we do all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying.
12.20: For I fear that when I come, I shall not find you as I would like - and that I shall not be found by you as you would like - and that there is strife, envying, wrath, rivalry, slander, gossip, pride, and discord;
12.21: that when I come again, my God humbles me among you. And I shall lament many of those who have sinned already and have not repented of the uncleanness and fornication and lewdness which they have committed.

13.1: This is the third time that I come to you. In the mouths of two or three witnesses shall every word stand.
13.2: I told you before, and tell you now beforehand, as though I had been present a second time. So I write now - being absent from those who until now have sinned, and to all others - that if I come again, I will not spare anyone;
13.3: since you seek proof of Christ speaking in me, Who is not weak toward you, but is mighty in you.
13.4: For though He was crucified through His weakness, yet He lives through the power of God. And we, no doubt, are weak in Him. But we shall live with Him, through the power of God, toward you.
13.5: Test yourselves, whether you are in the faith. Examine yourselves. Do you not know yourselves how that Jesus Christ is in you, unless you are disqualified?
13.6: But I trust that you shall know that we are not disqualified.
13.7: Now I pray to God that you do no evil; not that we should seem approved, but that you should do that which is honest, though we may be disqualified.
13.8: For we cannot do anything against the truth, but for the truth.
13.9: For we are glad when we are weak, and you are strong. For this also we pray: even your perfecting.
13.10: Therefore, I write these things while being absent ( so that when I am present, I should not use sharpness ) according to the power which the Lord has given me to edification, and not to destruction.
13.11: Finally brothers, farewell. Be perfect. Be of good comfort. Be of one mind. Live in peace. And the God of love and peace shall be with you.
13.12: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the Saints salute you.
13.13: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ - and the love of God - and the communion of the Holy Ghost be with you all. Amen. ( the second Epistle to the Corinthians written from Philippi - a city in Macedonia - and sent by Titus and Lucas )

1.1: Paul, an Apostle ( neither of men, nor by man; but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, Who has raised Him from the dead ),
1.2: And all the brothers who are with me, to the Churches of Galatia:
1.3: Grace be with you, and peace, from God the Father; and from our Lord Jesus Christ,
1.4: Who gave Himself for our sins; that He might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God, even our Father,
1.5: To Whom be glory, forever and ever, Amen.
1.6: I marvel that you are so soon lured away to another Gospel; from Him who had called you in the grace of Christ,
1.7: Which is not another Gospel. Yet, there are some who are agitating you, and intend to pervert the Gospel of Christ.
1.8: But even if we, or an angel from Heaven, preach to you any other gospel than that which we have preached, let him be accursed.
1.9: As we have said before, so say I now again: If anyone preaches to you any other gospel than that which you have received, let him be accursed.
1.10: For as of now, do I preach man’s doctrine, or God’s? Or, do I go about to please men? For if I were still pleasing men, I would not be the servant of Christ.
1.11: Now let it be known, brothers, that the Gospel which was preached by me, is not according to man.
1.12: Neither did I receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.
1.13: For you have heard of my former way of life in the Jewish religion; how I persecuted the Church of God extremely, and destroyed it,
1.14: And advanced in the Jewish religion above many of my countrymen and was much more devoted to the traditions of my fathers.
1.15: But when it pleased God ( who had set me apart from my mother’s womb, and called me by His grace )
1.16: To reveal his Son in me; that I should preach Him among the Gentiles immediately. I did not communicate with flesh and blood.
1.17: Nor did I return to Jerusalem, to those who were Apostles before me. But I went into Arabia and returned again to Damascus.
1.18: Then, after three years, I came again to Jerusalem, to visit Peter; and stayed with him fifteen days.
1.19: And I saw no other Apostle except James, the Lord’s brother.
1.20: Now the things which I write to you, behold, I testify before God, that I do not lie.
1.21: After that, I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia. For I was unknown by face to the Churches of Judea which are in Christ,
1.22: Who had only heard some say, “He who formerly persecuted us, now preaches the faith which before he destroyed. ”
1.23: And they glorified God in me.

2.1: Then, fourteen years after, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took with me Titus also.
2.2: And I went up by revelation and declared to them that Gospel which I preach among the Gentiles ( but privately to those who were the chief, lest by any means I should run - or had run - in vain ).
2.3: But not even Titus - who was with me, though he were a Grecian - was compelled to be circumcised,
2.4: This was because of the false brethren who were craftily sent in; and crept in privately to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might bring us into bondage.
2.5: But we gave them no place, not even for an hour, that the truth of the Gospel might continue with you.
2.6: But by those who seemed to be great, I was not taught ( whatever they were in time past, I am nothing the better; God accepts no man’s person ) For those who are the chief have added nothing to me above what I had.
2.7: But on the contrary, when they saw that the Gospel was committed to me over the uncircumcision, as the Gospel over the circumcision was to Peter:
2.8: ( For he who was mighty by Peter in the Apostleship over the circumcision, was also mighty by me toward the Gentiles. )
2.9: And when James and Cephas and John knew of the grace that was given to me - who are counted as pillars - they gave to me and to Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, that we should preach to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcision;
2.10: Warning only that we should remember the poor. Which I was also diligent to do.
2.11: And when Peter had come to Antioch, I opposed him to his face. For he was to be condemned.
2.12: For before certain ones came from James, he ate with the Gentiles. But when they had come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision.
2.13: And the other Jews likewise played the hypocrites with him. So much so that Barnabas was led away with them by their hypocrisy.
2.14: But when I saw that they did not go the right way to the truth of the Gospel, I said to Peter before all, “If you, being a Jew, live as the Gentiles, and not like the Jews, why constrain the Gentiles to do like the Jews?
2.15: We, who are Jews by birth and not Gentile sinners,
2.16: know that a man is not justified by the works of the Law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ. Even we, I say, have believed in Jesus Christ; that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the Law. Because, by the works of the Law, no flesh shall be justified.
2.17: If then, while we seek to be made righteous by Christ, we ourselves are found sinners, is Christ therefore the minister of sin? May it never be!
2.18: For if I build again the things that I have destroyed, I make myself a trespasser.
2.19: For I, through the Law, am dead to the Law, that I might live to God.
2.20: I am crucified with Christ, but I live; yet not I anymore, but Christ lives in me. And, in that I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith in the Son of God, Who has loved me, and given Himself for me.
2.21: I do not abrogate the grace of God. For if righteousness is by the Law, then Christ died for nothing. ”

3.1: O, foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you, that you should not obey the truth; before whose eyes Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified?
3.2: This only would I learn from you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the Law or by the hearing of faith?
3.3: Are you so foolish, that after you have begun in the Spirit, you would now be made perfect by the flesh?
3.4: Have you suffered so many things in vain, if so be it even in vain?
3.5: He, therefore, who ministers to you the Spirit, and works miracles among you, does he do it through the works of the Law, or by the hearing of faith?
3.6: Rather, as Abraham believed God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness,
3.7: know you therefore that those who are of faith, are the same children of Abraham.
3.8: For the Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles through faith, preached the Gospel to Abraham beforehand, saying, “In you shall all the Gentiles be blessed. ”
3.9: So then those who are of faith, are blessed with faithful Abraham.
3.10: For as many as are of the works of the Law, are under the curse. For it is written, “Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all things which are written in the book of the Law, to do them. ”
3.11: And it is evident that no one is justified by the Law, in the sight of God. For the just shall live by faith.
3.12: And the Law is not of faith: but the one who shall do those things, shall live in them.
3.13: Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the Law, being made a curse for us, ( for it is written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree” ).
3.14: That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Christ Jesus. That we might receive the promise of the Spirit, through faith.
3.15: Brothers, I speak as men do: Though it be but a man’s covenant, when it is confirmed, no one ignores it, or adds anything to it.
3.16: Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He does not say, “and to the seeds”, as speaking of many, but, “And to your seed”, as of one, which is Christ.
3.17: And this I say, that the covenant that was previously confirmed by God in Christ, cannot be annulled by the Law, which was four hundred and thirty years after; so that it should make the promise of no effect.
3.18: For if the inheritance is of the Law, it is no more by the promise. But God gave it freely to Abraham by promise.
3.19: Why, then, the Law? It was added because of the transgressions; till the seed came, to which the promise was made. And it was ordained by Angels in the hand of a Mediator.
3.20: However, there is no Mediator of one. But God is one.
3.21: Is the Law, then, against the promises of God? Never may it be! For if there had been a Law given which could have given life, surely righteousness should have been by the Law.
3.22: But the Scripture has confined all under sin, that the promise, by faith in Jesus Christ, should be given to those who believe.
3.23: But before faith came, we were kept under the Law, as under guard, and locked up, until that faith which should be revealed.
3.24: So that the Law was our tutor, bringing us to Christ, that we might be made righteous by faith.
3.25: But after that faith has come, we are no longer under a tutor.
3.26: For you are all the sons of God by faith, in Christ Jesus.
3.27: For all you who were baptized into Christ, have put on Christ.
3.28: There is neither Jew nor Grecian. There is neither bond nor free. There is neither male nor female. For you are all one in Christ Jesus.
3.29: And if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed, and heirs by promise.

4.1: Then I say that the heir ( as long as he is a child ) differs nothing from a servant - though he be Lord of all -
4.2: but is under tutors and governors until the time appointed by the Father.
4.3: Even so, we ( when we were children ) were in bondage under the basic principles of the world.
4.4: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman and made under the Law;
4.5: so that He might redeem those who were under the Law ( that we might receive adoption as sons ).
4.6: And because you are sons, God has sent forth the Spirit of His Son into your hearts, who cries, “Abba, Father! ”
4.7: Therefore, you are a servant no more, but a son. Now, if you are a son, you are also the heir of God, through Christ.
4.8: But even then, when you did not know God, you were enslaved by those who, by nature, are not gods.
4.9: But now, seeing you know God - indeed, rather, are known by God - how can you turn again to weak and poor principals; so that, as before, you will be in bondage again?
4.10: You observe days and months and times and years.
4.11: I am in fear for you, lest I have bestowed upon you labor in vain.
4.12: Be as me, brothers, I beg you ( for I am also like you ). You have not hurt me at all.
4.13: And you know how through weakness of the flesh I preached the Gospel to you at first.
4.14: And your trial from me ( which was in my flesh ) you neither despised nor abhorred. But you received me as an angel of God; indeed, as Christ Jesus.
4.15: Where then is your felicity? For I bear witness that if it had been possible, you would have plucked out your own eyes and have given them to me.
4.16: Have I therefore become your enemy because I tell you the truth?
4.17: They are wrongly jealous for you. Yea, they would separate you from us, so that you would be jealous for them.
4.18: But it is a good thing to always love earnestly in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you,
4.19: my little children with whom I travail in birth again, until Christ is formed in you.
4.20: And I would that I were with you now, so I might change my voice. For I am in doubt of you.
4.21: Tell me, you who would be under the Law, do you not hear the Law?
4.22: For it is written that Abraham had two sons: one by a servant and one by a free woman.
4.23: But he who was by the servant was born after the flesh. And he who was by the free woman was born by promise.
4.24: These things are allegorical. For these mothers are the two Testaments. The one called Hagar begat those of mount Sinai, who are enslaved.
4.25: For Hagar ( or Sinai ) is a mountain in Arabia, and it is now presently Jerusalem. And she is enslaved with her children.
4.26: But the Jerusalem above is free and is the mother of us all.
4.27: For it is written, “Rejoice, you barren who bear no children! Break forth, and cry, you who do not travail! For the desolate has many more children than she who has a husband. ”
4.28: Therefore, brothers, we are like Isaac: children of the promise.
4.29: But just as at that time the one who was born after the flesh persecuted the one who was born after the Spirit, so also it is now.
4.30: But what says the Scripture? ‘Put out the servant and her son. For the son of the servant shall not be heir with the son of the free woman. ’
4.31: Then, brothers, we are not children of the servant, but of the free woman.

5.1: Stand fast, therefore, in the liberty whereby Christ has made us free. And be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.
5.2: Behold, I, Paul, say to you, that if you shall become circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.
5.3: For I testify again to every man who is circumcised, that he is under obligation to keep the whole Law.
5.4: You are severed from Christ. Whoever is justified by the Law, you are fallen from grace.
5.5: For we, through the Spirit, wait for the hope of righteousness through faith.
5.6: For in Jesus Christ, neither circumcision nor uncircumcision avails anything, but faith ( which works by love ).
5.7: You were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth?
5.8: It is not the persuasion of the One who calls you.
5.9: A little leaven leavens the whole lump.
5.10: I have confidence in you, through the Lord, that you will be single - minded. But he who troubles you shall bear condemnation, whoever he might be.
5.11: And I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision, why do I still suffer persecution? Then the stumbling block of the cross is abolished.
5.12: I even wish those who disquiet you would emasculate themselves.
5.13: For brothers, you have been called to freedom. Only, do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but by love serve one another.
5.14: For all the Law is fulfilled in one word, which is this: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself. ”
5.15: If, however, you bite and devour one another, take heed, for you might be consumed by one another.
5.16: Then I say, walk in the Spirit, and you shall not fulfill the lusts of the flesh.
5.17: For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh. And these are contrary one to another, so that you cannot do the things you would like.
5.18: And if you be led by the Spirit, you are not under the Law.
5.19: Moreover, the works of the flesh are obvious: adultery, fornication, impurity, lewdness,
5.20: idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalry, dissensions, heresies,
5.21: envy, murders, drunkenness, gluttony, and the like. And, just as I have told you before, those who do such things shall not inherit the Kingdom of God.
5.22: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
5.23: gentleness, self - control. Against such things there is no law.
5.24: For those who are Christ’s, have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
5.25: If we live in the Spirit, we should also walk in the Spirit.
5.26: Let us not become boastful, provoking one another, envying one another.

6.1: Brothers, even if a man should be overcome in some offense, you who are spiritual restore such one with the spirit of humility, considering yourself, lest you also be tempted.
6.2: Bear one another’s burden, and so fulfill the Law of Christ.
6.3: For if anyone seems to himself something, when he is nothing. He deceives himself.
6.4: But let everyone test his own work. And then shall he boast in himself only and not in another.
6.5: For everyone shall bear his own burden.
6.6: Let the one who is taught in the word make the one who has taught him a partaker of all good things.
6.7: Be not deceived. God is not mocked. For whatever a man sows, that shall he also reap.
6.8: For the one who sows to his flesh, shall reap destruction of the flesh. But the one who sows to the Spirit, shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.
6.9: Let us not, therefore, be weary of well - doing. For in due season, we shall reap, if we do not grow weary.
6.10: Therefore, while we have time, let us do good to all; and now especially to those who are of the household of the faith.
6.11: You see how large the letters are which I have written to you with my own hand.
6.12: As many as desire to have a fair appearance in the flesh, they urge you to be circumcised, only because they would not suffer persecution for the cross of Christ.
6.13: For they themselves who are circumcised do not keep the Law, but desire to have you circumcised, so that they might boast in your flesh.
6.14: But may it never be that I should boast in anything but the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ; whereby the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world!
6.15: For in Christ Jesus, neither circumcision nor uncircumcision avails anything, but a new creature.
6.16: And as many as walk according to this rule, peace shall be upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
6.17: From henceforth let no one give me trouble. For I bear on my body the marks of the Lord Jesus.
6.18: Brothers, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen. ( to the Galatians; written from Rome. )

1.1: Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, To the saints who are at Ephesus and to the faithful in Christ Jesus:
1.2: Grace be with you, and peace, from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: Blessed be God, and the Father of our Lord, Jesus Christ, Who has blessed us with all spiritual blessing in the Heavenly realms in Christ,
1.4: as He has chosen us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before Him in love;
1.5: having predestined us to be adopted, through Jesus Christ, to Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will,
1.6: to the praise of the glory of His grace, which He has freely bestowed on us in the Beloved;
1.7: in whom we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of His grace,
1.8: with which He has been abundant toward us in all wisdom and understanding;
1.9: and has made known to us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure, which He has purposed in Him.
1.10: That in the dispensation of the fullness of the times, He might gather together all things in Christ, both in Heaven and on Earth;
1.11: in Whom we also have obtained an inheritance, being predestined according to the purpose of Him who works all things according the counsel of His own will,
1.12: that we who first trusted in Christ, should be to the praise of His glory;
1.13: in whom also, you, having heard the word of truth, the Gospel of your salvation, and after having believed, were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
1.14: Who is the guarantee of our inheritance, for the redemption of that acquired possession, to the praise of His glory.
1.15: Therefore, also, after I heard of the faith which you have in the Lord Jesus, and love toward all the saints,
1.16: I do not cease to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers,
1.17: that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, might give to you the Spirit of wisdom and revelation through the knowledge of Him,
1.18: that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened, so that you may know what the hope is of His calling, and what the riches are of His glorious inheritance in the saints,
1.19: and what is the exceeding greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of His strength;
1.20: which He worked in Christ when He raised him from the dead, and set Him at His right hand in the Heavenly realms,
1.21: far above every principality and power and might and domination, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in the coming one.
1.22: And all things have been put under His feet. And He has been given headship over all things of the church,
1.23: which is His body - the fullness of Him Who fills all in all.

2.1: And you were dead in trespasses and sins
2.2: ( wherein you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the authority of the ruler of the air, even the spirit who now works in the sons of disobedience,
2.3: among whom all of us also once lived in the lusts of our flesh, in fulfilling the will of the flesh, and of the mind; and were, by nature, the children of wrath, just as the rest ).
2.4: But God, Who is rich in mercy, through His great love with which He loved us,
2.5: even when we were dead by sins, has quickened us together in Christ ( by grace you are saved )
2.6: and has raised us up together and made us sit together in the Heavenly places in Christ Jesus;
2.7: so that He might show, in the ages to come, the exceeding riches of His grace through His kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.
2.8: For by grace are you saved, through faith, and that not of yourselves. It is the gift from God
2.9: ( not of works, lest anyone should boast ).
2.10: For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works; which God has ordained, so that we would walk in them.
2.11: Therefore, remember that you, being formerly Gentiles in the flesh ( the ones called “uncircumcision” by those called “circumcision” in the flesh, made with hands ),
2.12: that you were, at that time, without Christ; and were aliens from the commonwealth of Israel; and were strangers to the covenants of the promise; and had no hope; and were without God in the world.
2.13: But now, in Christ Jesus, you who were once far off, are made near by the blood of Christ.
2.14: For He is our peace. He has made of both, one, and has broken the barrier of hostility;
2.15: having annulled ( through His flesh ) the Law of commandments contained in ordinances, in order to make ( in Himself ) one new man from the two. And so, make peace,
2.16: so that He might reconcile both to God in one body by the cross, and thereby slay hostility.
2.17: And He came and preached peace to you who were afar off, and to those who were near.
2.18: For through Him we both have access to the Father, by one Spirit.
2.19: Now therefore, you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but citizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
2.20: having been built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief cornerstone;
2.21: In Him, all the building, fitted together, grows into a holy Temple in the Lord.
2.22: In Him, you also are being built together, to be the habitation of God by the Spirit.

3.1: For this reason, I, Paul, am the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles.
3.2: If indeed you have heard of the stewardship of the grace of God, which is given to me toward you.
3.3: So that God, by revelation, has shown this mystery to me ( as I briefly wrote before;
3.4: by which, when you read it, you may know my understanding of the mystery of Christ,
3.5: which was not made known to the sons of men in other ages as it is now revealed to His holy Apostles and Prophets by the Spirit ),
3.6: So that the Gentiles should also be inheritors of the same body, and partakers of His promise in Christ, by the Gospel;
3.7: whereof I am made a minister by the gift of the grace of God ( given to me through the working of His power ).
3.8: To me, the least of all saints, is this grace given, so that I would preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ;
3.9: and make clear to all what the stewardship of the mystery is ( which from the beginning of the world has been hid in God, Who has created all things by Jesus Christ );
3.10: to the intent that now the manifold wisdom of God might be made known by the church to principalities and powers in Heavenly realms,
3.11: according to the eternal purpose which He made in Christ Jesus our Lord;
3.12: By Him we have boldness and confident access, through faith in Him.
3.13: Therefore, I desire that you do not grow weary of my tribulations for you ( which is your glory ).
3.14: For this reason I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
3.15: ( from Whom is named every family in Heaven and on Earth )
3.16: so that He might grant - according to the riches of His glory - that you be strengthened by His Spirit in the inner man;
3.17: So that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith;
3.18: so that you, being rooted and grounded in love, may be able to comprehend ( with all saints ) what is the breadth and length and depth and height;
3.19: and to know the love of Christ which surpasses knowledge. So that you may be filled with all fullness of God.
3.20: Now therefore, to the one who is able to do all things exceedingly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us;
3.21: to Him be praise in the church and in Christ Jesus, throughout all generations, forever. Amen.

4.1: I, therefore, being the prisoner in the Lord, exhort you to walk worthily of the calling to which you were called,
4.2: with all humility and gentleness; with patience, bearing with one another in love,
4.3: being diligent to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
4.4: There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called into one hope of your vocation;
4.5: one Lord, one Faith, one Baptism,
4.6: one God and Father of all, Who is above all, and through all, and in all.
4.7: But to every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
4.8: Therefore it says, “When He ascended upon high, He captured captivity, and gave gifts to men.
4.9: ( Now, in that He ascended, what is it but that He had also descended first into the lowest parts of the earth?
4.10: He Who descended is also the same Who ascended far above all heavens, so that He might complete all things. )
4.11: He, indeed, gave some to be Apostles, and some Prophets, and some Evangelists, and some Pastors, and Teachers,
4.12: for the preparing of the Saints, for the work of the ministry, and for the edification of the body of Christ,
4.13: until we all reach the unity of faith and the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature belonging to the fullness of Christ;
4.14: So that we are henceforth children no more, wavering and carried about with every wind of doctrine and by the deceit of men who with craftiness lay in wait to deceive.
4.15: But let us follow the truth in love. And in all things grow up into Him Who is the Head, Christ;
4.16: by Whom all the body, being coupled and knit together by the supply of every joint, according to the measure of each individual part, makes increase to the body, to the edifying of itself in love.
4.17: This I say, therefore, and testify in the Lord: that you henceforth do not walk as other Gentiles walk ( in the frivolity of their mind,
4.18: having their understanding darkened, and being strangers to the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the hardness of their heart );
4.19: who, having grown numb to all feeling, have given themselves over to lewdness for the working of uncleanness with all greediness.
4.20: But, you have not so learned Christ,
4.21: if indeed you have heard Him, and have been taught by Him, just as truth is in Jesus.
4.22: As for your past life, you are to cast off the old man who is being corrupted through deceitful desires,
4.23: and be renewed in the spirit of your mind.
4.24: And put on the new man, who has been created according to God for righteousness and true holiness.
4.25: Therefore, having laid aside lying, everyone speak truth to his neighbor. For we are members one of another.
4.26: Be angry, but do not sin. Do not let the sun go down upon your irritation,
4.27: nor give place to the devil.
4.28: Let him who stole, steal no more. But rather, let him labor and work with his hands that which is good, so that he may have something to give to those in need.
4.29: Let no worthless word proceed out of your mouth, but only if it is good for edification, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
4.30: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in Whom you are sealed for the Day of Redemption.
4.31: Let all bitterness and fury and anger, clamor, and slander be taken from you, along with all wickedness.
4.32: Be kind one to another, and tender - hearted, freely forgiving one another; even as God, for Christ’s sake, freely forgave you.

5.1: Therefore, be imitators of God, as beloved children.
5.2: And walk in love, just as Christ has loved us and has given Himself for us as an offering and a sacrifice of a sweet - smelling savor to God.
5.3: But do not let fornication and all uncleanness or covetousness even be named among you ( as is also becoming to saints ),
5.4: nor filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor coarse joking ( which are not fitting ); but rather the giving of thanks.
5.5: For this you know: that no fornicator, nor impure or covetous person, who is an idolater, has any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ, and of God.
5.6: Let no one deceive you with empty words. For the wrath of God comes upon the children of disobedience.
5.7: Therefore, do not be companions with them.
5.8: For you were once darkness but are now light in the Lord. Walk as children of light.
5.9: For the fruit of the light is in all goodness and righteousness and truth,
5.10: approving that which is pleasing to the Lord.
5.11: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness. But rather, even expose them.
5.12: For it is shameful even to speak of the things which are done by them in secret.
5.13: But all things, when they are exposed by the light, are made visible. For it is light that makes all things visible.
5.14: Therefore it says, “Awake, you who sleep. And stand up from the dead. And Christ shall shine upon you. ”
5.15: Be mindful, therefore, that you walk carefully - not as fools, but as wise -
5.16: redeeming the season. For the days are evil.
5.17: Therefore, be not unwise. But, understand what the will of the Lord is.
5.18: And do not be drunk with wine ( wherein is wastefulness ). But, be filled with the Spirit,
5.19: speaking to yourselves in Psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody to the Lord in your hearts,
5.20: giving thanks always, for all things, to God, even the Father, in the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ,
5.21: submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God.
5.22: Wives, submit yourselves to your husbands, as to the Lord.
5.23: For the husband is the wife’s head, even as Christ is the head of the Church. And the same is the Savior of the body.
5.24: But, as the Church is in subjection to Christ, so also let the wives be to their husbands in everything.
5.25: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ loved the Church, and gave Himself for her;
5.26: so that He might sanctify her and cleanse her by the washing of water through the word,
5.27: So that He might make her a glorious Church to Himself, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing. But that it should be holy and without blame.
5.28: So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife, loves himself.
5.29: For no one ever yet hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, even as the Lord does the Church.
5.30: For we are members of his body, of His flesh and of His bones.
5.31: For this cause shall a man leave father and mother and shall cling to his wife. And the two shall be one flesh.
5.32: This is a great secret. But I speak concerning Christ and concerning the church.
5.33: Yet, let every one of you do the same. Let everyone love his wife, even as himself. And let the wife see that she fears her husband.

6.1: Children, obey your parents in the Lord. For this is right.
6.2: Honor your father and mother ( which is the first commandment with a promise ),
6.3: so that it may be well with you and that you may live long on earth.
6.4: And, fathers, do not provoke your children to anger. But bring them up in the training and admonition of the Lord.
6.5: Servants, be obedient to your masters, according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in simplicity of heart, as unto Christ;
6.6: not with service to the eye ( as men - pleasers ) but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart
6.7: with good will, serving the Lord and not men.
6.8: And know that whatever good thing anyone does, that same shall he receive from the Lord, whether slave or free.
6.9: And masters, do the same things to them, giving up threatening and knowing that your master also is in Heaven. And there is no partiality with Him.
6.10: Finally, my brothers, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of His might.
6.11: Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the deceit of the devil.
6.12: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against the kings, against the authorities, and against the rulers of the darkness of this world; against the spiritual forces of iniquity which are in the high place.
6.13: For this reason take up the whole armor of God, so that you may be able to withstand on the evil day. And having finished all things, stand fast.
6.14: Stand therefore, having wrapped your waist with truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness.
6.15: And shod your feet with the preparation of the Gospel of peace.
6.16: Above all, take the shield of Faith, with which you may quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.
6.17: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
6.18: And pray always, with all manner of prayer and supplication, in the Spirit. And watch for this very thing - with all perseverance and supplication - for all Saints
6.19: and for me; that a word may be given to me, so that I may open my mouth boldly to make known the secret of the Gospel,
6.20: for which I am an ambassador in a chain. So that therein I may speak boldly as I ought to speak.
6.21: And so that you may also know my affairs ( and what I do ) Tychicus, my dear brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things.
6.22: I have sent him to you for this very purpose, so that you might know my affairs and that he might comfort your hearts.
6.23: Peace to the brothers and love with faith, from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
6.24: Grace be with all those who love our Lord Jesus Christ incorruptibly. Amen. ( written from Rome to the Ephesians and sent by Tychicus. )

1.1: Paul and Timothy, the servants of Jesus Christ, To all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, with the elders and deacons:
1.2: Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: I thank my God with every remembrance of you,
1.4: ( always, in all my prayers for all you, praying with joy ),
1.5: because of the fellowship which you have in the Gospel, from the first day until now.
1.6: And I am persuaded of this same thing: that He who has begun this good work in you will perfect it until the Day of Jesus Christ;
1.7: just as it is right for me to think this way of you all, because I have you in my heart, since both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the Gospel you all were fellow partakers of grace with me.
1.8: For God is my witness how I long after you all with the affection of Jesus Christ.
1.9: And this I pray: that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment;
1.10: so that you may test those things which are better; that you may be pure and without offense until the Day of Christ,
1.11: filled with the fruit of righteousness which is by Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
1.12: Brothers, I desire that you understand that the things which are against me have really caused a furthering of the Gospel.
1.13: So, as for my bonds in Christ, they are famous throughout all the Praetorium and in all other places;
1.14: so much so that many of the brothers in the Lord are emboldened by my bonds and dare speak the word of God more frankly.
1.15: Indeed, some preach Christ out of envy and strife, but some also out of goodwill.
1.16: Indeed, the former preaches Christ out of rivalry ( and not purely, supposing to add more affliction to my bonds ),
1.17: but the latter out of love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the Gospel.
1.18: What then? Christ is still preached in all manner of ways, whether under a pretense or sincerely. And I rejoice in that! Indeed, and I will rejoice!
1.19: For I know that this shall cause my deliverance ( through your prayer and by the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ )
1.20: as I fervently expect and hope that in nothing shall I be ashamed. But that with all confidence ( as always ) so now Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether it be by life or by death.
1.21: For, to me, Christ is life and death is gain.
1.22: But if living in the flesh brings fruit from my labor, what shall I choose? I do not know!
1.23: For I am caught between both desiring to be released and to be with Christ ( which is best of all ).
1.24: Nevertheless, to abide in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
1.25: And of this I am sure: that I shall stay and continue with you all for the progress and joy of your faith,
1.26: so that by my coming to you again your boasting in Jesus Christ may abound through me.
1.27: Only conduct yourselves as it becomes the Gospel of Christ; so that whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear of your matters that you continue in one spirit and in one mind, striving together for the faith of the Gospel.
1.28: And be frightened in nothing by your adversaries ( which is to them a proof of destruction - but to you of salvation - and this from God! ).
1.29: For to you it is given concerning Christ that not only should you believe in Him, but also to suffer concerning Him,
1.30: having the same fight which you saw in me and now hear of in me.

2.1: Therefore, if there is any encouragement in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any compassion and affection,
2.2: fulfill my joy; so that you are like - minded, having the same love, being of one accord and of one judgment.
2.3: So that nothing is done through self - interest or empty pride. But that in humility, everyone thinks others better than himself.
2.4: Do not be preoccupied with your own things, but rather with the things of others.
2.5: Let the same mind be in you that was in Christ Jesus;
2.6: Who, being in the form of God, did not eagerly desire equality with God as a prize.
2.7: But He emptied Himself and took on the form of a servant ( and the likeness of a man, having been made ).
2.8: He humbled Himself and became obedient to the death - even the death of the cross.
2.9: Therefore, God has highly exalted Him and given Him a Name above every Name.
2.10: That at the Name of Jesus, every knee should bow: in Heaven, and on Earth, and under the Earth.
2.11: And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is the Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
2.12: Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed me - not only in my presence, but now much more so in my absence - work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
2.13: For it is God who works in you - both in your will and in your works - according to His good pleasure.
2.14: Do all things without grumbling or disputing,
2.15: so that you may be blameless and pure children of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a perverted and crooked nation ( among whom you shine as lights in the world ),
2.16: Hold forth the word of life, so that I may rejoice on the day of Christ that I have not run for nothing or labored for nothing.
2.17: Indeed, and though I am being poured out as a drink offering upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I am glad and rejoice with you all!
2.18: And likewise also, you be glad and rejoice with me!
2.19: And I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you shortly, so that I also may be encouraged when I know your state.
2.20: For I have no one of like mind who will faithfully care for your matters.
2.21: For all seek their own, and not that which is Jesus Christ’s.
2.22: But you know the proof of him who, as a child with his father, has served with me in the Gospel.
2.23: Therefore, I hope to send him as soon as I know how it will go with me.
2.24: And I trust in the Lord that I, myself, shall also come shortly.
2.25: But I thought it necessary to send to you my brother, fellow laborer, and fellow soldier, Epaphroditus ( who is now your messenger and minister to my needs ).
2.26: For he longed after all of you, and was full of heaviness, because you had heard that he had been sick.
2.27: And no doubt he was sick, very near to death. But God had mercy on him; and not on him only, but on me also, so that I should not have sorrow upon sorrow.
2.28: Therefore, I sent him all the more speedily, so that when you would see him again you might rejoice and I might be the less sorrowful.
2.29: Therefore, receive him in the Lord with all joy. And value such men highly.
2.30: Because he was near death for the work of Christ and did not regard his life, to fulfill that service which was lacking on your part toward me.

3.1: Moreover, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord! It does not trouble me to write the same things to you. And for you it is certain.
3.2: Beware of dogs. Beware of evil workers. Beware of the concision.
3.3: For we are the circumcision. We worship God in the Spirit and rejoice in Christ Jesus and have no confidence in the flesh,
3.4: though I might also have confidence in the flesh. If anyone else thinks that he might have confidence in the flesh, more so I:
3.5: circumcised the eighth day; of the kindred of Israel; of the tribe of Benjamin; a Hebrew of Hebrews; by the Law, a Pharisee;
3.6: concerning zeal, I persecuted the Church; according to righteousness ( which is in the Law ), I had become blameless.
3.7: But whatever things that were gain to me, the same I have counted as loss for Christ’s sake.
3.8: Indeed, also, I count all things but loss for the sake of the surpassing knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for Whom I have counted all things loss and judge them to be garbage, so that I may gain Christ
3.9: and be found in Him; that is, not having my own righteousness ( which is of the Law ) but that which is through faith in Christ - the righteousness which is from God by faith;
3.10: so that I may know Him and the power of His resurrection and the fellowship of His suffering and be conformed to His death
3.11: ( if by any means I might attain to the resurrection from the dead ).
3.12: Not that I have already attained to it or been perfected. But I follow, so that I may seize that for which I also was seized by Christ Jesus.
3.13: Brothers, I do not count myself as having seized it. But one thing I do: I forget that which is behind and stretch forward toward that which is ahead;
3.14: and follow hard toward the mark, for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
3.15: Let us, therefore ( as many as are mature ) be thus - minded. And if you are otherwise - minded, even this God shall reveal to you.
3.16: Nevertheless, to that which we have already attained, let us walk by one rule and be of the same mind.
3.17: Brothers, be imitators of me and observe those who also walk thus ( as you have us for an example ).
3.18: For many walk of whom I have often told you ( and tell you now, weeping ) who are the enemies of the cross of Christ;
3.19: whose end is destruction; whose God is their belly; and whose glory is in their knowledge of earthly things, to their shame.
3.20: But our citizenship is in Heaven, from where we also look for the Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
3.21: He shall transform our humiliated body into a body conformed to His glory, according to the working whereby He is able even to subdue all things to Himself.

4.1: Therefore, my brothers, beloved and longed for, my joy and my crown, so continue in the Lord, beloved.
4.2: I encourage Euodia and I encourage Syntyche to be of the same mind in the Lord.
4.3: Indeed and I ask you also, faithful colleague, to help these women who labored with me in the Gospel, with Clement also, and with other of my fellow laborers, whose names are in the Book of Life.
4.4: Rejoice in the Lord always. I say again, rejoice!
4.5: Let your gentleness be known to all. The Lord is near!
4.6: Be anxious about nothing. But in all things, let your requests be made known to God in prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving.
4.7: And the peace of God - which surpasses all understanding - shall guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.
4.8: Finally, brothers, whatever things are true; whatever things are noble; whatever things are right; whatever things are pure; whatever things are lovely; whatever things are admirable; if there is any excellence or if there is any praise, think on these things.
4.9: That also which you have learned and received, and have heard and seen in me, those things do. And the God of Peace shall be with you.
4.10: But, I also rejoice greatly in the Lord that now at last your care for me springs afresh. Though you did care before, you lacked opportunity.
4.11: I do not speak because of need. For I have learned to be content in whatever state I am.
4.12: Also, I know how to be brought low and I know how to abound. Everywhere, and in all things, I have learned the secret of being full and of being hungry; of abounding and of having need.
4.13: I have strength for all things through Christ Who empowers me.
4.14: Nevertheless, you have done well to share in my affliction.
4.15: And you, Philippians, also know that in the beginning of the Gospel ( when I departed from Macedonia ) no church partnered with me in the matter of giving and receiving, except you.
4.16: For even when I was in Thessalonica, you sent once and then again for my needs.
4.17: Not that I desire a gift. But I desire the fruit which overflows to your account.
4.18: However, I have received all and have plenty. I am full, having received from Epaphroditus that which came from you - a sweet - smelling sacrifice, acceptable and well - pleasing to God.
4.19: And my God will fulfill all your needs through His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
4.20: Now, to God our Father be praise for ever and ever. Amen.
4.21: Greet all the Saints in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me greet you.
4.22: All the saints greet you, and most of all those who are of Caesar’s household.
4.23: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen. ( written to the Philippians from Rome and sent by Epaphroditus. )

1.1: Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, and Timothy, our brother,
1.2: To those who are at Colosse, saints and faithful brothers in Christ: Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: We give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, always praying for you,
1.4: having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of your love toward all saints,
1.5: because of the hope which is laid up for you in Heaven; of which you have heard before by the word of truth, which is the Gospel.
1.6: It has come to you even as it has to all the world and is fruitful, as it was also among you from the day that you heard and truly knew the grace of God;
1.7: as you also learned from Epaphras ( our dear fellow servant ), who is for you a faithful minister of Christ.
1.8: He has also declared to us your love in the Spirit.
1.9: For this reason, we also ( since the day we heard of it ) do not cease to pray for you and to desire that you might be fulfilled with knowledge of His will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;
1.10: so that you might walk worthily of the Lord and please Him in all things, being fruitful in all good works and increasing in the knowledge of God;
1.11: strengthened with all might through His glorious power, leading to all patience and endurance with joy;
1.12: giving thanks to the Father Who has qualified us to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light;
1.13: Who has delivered us from the power of darkness and has transferred us into the Kingdom of His dear Son
1.14: ( in Whom we have redemption through His blood; that is, the forgiveness of sins ).
1.15: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creation.
1.16: For by Him were all things created which are in Heaven and which are on Earth - things visible and invisible - whether thrones or dominions or rulers or powers. All things were created through Him and for Him.
1.17: And He is before all things. And in Him all things consist.
1.18: And He is the Head of the body of the Church. He is the Beginning; Firstborn from the dead; so that in all things He might have preeminence.
1.19: For in Him was all fullness pleased to dwell.
1.20: And through Him were all things reconciled to Himself, having made peace by the blood of His cross; through Him, I say, whether things on Earth or things in Heaven.
1.21: And you also - who were in times past estranged and hostile because your minds were set on evil works - He has now reconciled
1.22: in the body of His flesh through death; to present you as holy and blameless and beyond reproach in His sight
1.23: if you continue to be grounded and established in the faith and are not moved away from the hope of the Gospel which you have heard ( having been preached to all creation under Heaven, and to which I, Paul, am a minister ).
1.24: Now, I rejoice in my sufferings for you and fulfill in my flesh the rest of the afflictions of Christ for His body’s sake ( which is the Church
1.25: and whereof I am a minister ) according to the dispensation of God which has been given me toward you to fulfill the word of God;
1.26: and which is the mystery hidden from all ages and generations and now made visible to his saints;
1.27: to whom God would make known the riches of His glorious mystery among the Gentiles – which is Christ in you, the hope of glory;
1.28: whom we preach, admonishing everyone, and teaching everyone in all wisdom, that we may present everyone complete in Christ Jesus.
1.29: Toward this I also toil, striving according to His miraculous power working in me.

2.1: For I desire that you knew what great struggle I have for you, and for those of Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;
2.2: that their hearts might be encouraged, having been joined together in love and in all the riches of the full assurance of understanding to know the mystery of God and the Father and of Christ,
2.3: in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
2.4: And this I say so that no one should deceive you with persuasive words.
2.5: For though I am absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in spirit, rejoicing and seeing your order and your steadfast faith in Christ.
2.6: Therefore, as you have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in Him;
2.7: being rooted and built up in Him and established in the faith as you have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.
2.8: Beware, lest anyone spoil you through philosophy and empty deceit according to the traditions of men, according to the principles of the world and not according to Christ.
2.9: For in Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily.
2.10: And you are complete in Him Who is the head of all principality and power.
2.11: In Him also are you circumcised with circumcision made without hands by putting off the sinful body of the flesh through the circumcision of Christ,
2.12: buried with Him in baptism ( in which you are also risen with Him through the faith of the working of God, Who raised Him from the dead ).
2.13: And you, who were dead in sins and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, He has made alive together with Him, forgiving all trespasses
2.14: and blotting out the handwriting of the ordinances against us which opposed us. He has taken it out of the way and fastened it upon the cross.
2.15: And having disarmed the rulers and authorities, and having made a show of them openly, He has triumphed over them in it.
2.16: Therefore, let no one judge you as regards food and drink, or regarding a holy day or the new moon or the Sabbath,
2.17: which are a shadow of things to come. But the body is of Christ.
2.18: Let no one, at his pleasure, bear rule over you by his humbleness of mind and his worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he has never seen, being rashly puffed up with his fleshly mind
2.19: and not taking hold of the Head ( from Whom all the body, supplied and knit together by joints and bonds, grows with a growth that is from God ).
2.20: Therefore, if you have died with Christ from the principles of the world, why then ( as though you lived in the world ) do you submit to ordinances such as:
2.22: which all perish with use and are according to the commandments and doctrines of men?
2.23: These things indeed have an appearance of wisdom and of voluntary religion and humbleness of mind and of not sparing the body but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.

3.1: If you, then, are risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sits at the right hand of God.
3.2: Set your mind on things which are above, not on things which are on the earth.
3.3: For you have died, and your life has been hidden with Christ in God.
3.4: When Christ ( Who is your life ) is revealed, then you shall also be revealed with Him in glory.
3.5: Therefore, mortify those parts of your body which are of the earth: fornication, impurity, depraved passions, lust, and covetousness ( which is idolatry ),
3.6: for the sake of which things the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience;
3.7: and wherein also you once walked when you lived in them.
3.8: But now, however, take all these things out of your mouth also: anger, wrath, malice, slander, foul language.
3.9: Do not lie to one another, having put off the old man with his deeds
3.10: and having put on the new ( who is renewed in knowledge after the image of Him who created him ).
3.11: There is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, slave, free; but all, and in all, is Christ.
3.12: Now, therefore, as the Elect of God, holy and beloved, put on hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience,
3.13: bearing with one another and forgiving one another. If anyone has a quarrel with another, even as Christ forgave, so do you.
3.14: And above all these things put on love, which is the bond of complete unity.
3.15: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which you were called in one body. And be thankful.
3.16: Let the word of Christ dwell in you abundantly, in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing each other in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with a grace in your hearts to God.
3.17: And whatever you shall do, in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
3.18: Wives, submit yourselves to your husbands, as it is fitting in the Lord.
3.19: Husbands, love your wives, and do not be embittered toward them.
3.20: Children, obey your parents in all things, for that is well - pleasing to the Lord.
3.21: Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, lest they be discouraged.
3.22: Servants, in all things, be obedient to those who are your masters according to the flesh; not with eye - service as men - pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God.
3.23: And whatever you do, work from your soul, as to the Lord, and not to men;
3.24: knowing that you shall receive the reward of the inheritance from the Lord. You serve the Lord Christ.
3.25: But the one who does wrong shall be repaid for the wrong that he has done. And there is no respect of persons.

4.1: Masters, do to your servants that which is just and equal, knowing that you also have a master in Heaven.
4.2: Be steadfast in prayer, watching with thanksgiving;
4.3: praying also for us that God may open a door of utterance to us to speak the mystery of Christ ( because of which I am also in bonds );
4.4: that I should make it clear as it behooves me to speak.
4.5: Walk wisely toward those who are outside, rescuing lost time.
4.6: Let your speech always be gracious, having been seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer each one.
4.7: Tychicus, our beloved brother and faithful minister and fellow servant in the Lord, shall make known to you my whole state.
4.8: I have sent him to you for the same purpose, so that he might know your state and might comfort your hearts
4.9: with Onesimus, a faithful and a beloved brother, who is one of you. They shall make known to you all things here.
4.10: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, salutes you; and Marcus, Barnabas’ cousin ( concerning whom you received the commandment: ‘If he comes to you, receive him. ’ );
4.11: and Jesus, who is called Justus. These are my only fellow workers for the Kingdom of God who are of the circumcision. They have been a comfort to me.
4.12: Epaphras, the servant of Christ ( who is one of you ) greets you and always contends for you in prayers - that you may stand perfect and full in all the will of God.
4.13: For I bear witness of him, that he has a great zeal for you and for those of Laodicea and those of Hierapolis.
4.14: Luke, the beloved physician, greets you; and Demas.
4.15: Greet the brothers who are of Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the church which is in his house.
4.16: And when this letter is read among you, have it read in the church of the Laodiceans also, and that you likewise read the letter written from Laodicea.
4.17: And say to Archippus, ‘Pay attention to the ministry that you have received in the Lord, so that you may fulfill it. ’
4.18: This greeting is by the hand of me, Paul. Remember my chains. Grace be with you. Amen. ( written from Rome to the Colossians, and sent by Tychicus, and Onesimus. )

1.1: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, To the Church of the Thessalonians, which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace be with you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.2: We always give God thanks for you all, making mention of you in our prayers,
1.3: unceasingly remembering your work of faith and diligent love and the patience of your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ ( in the sight of God our Father ),
1.4: knowing - beloved brothers - that you are the Elect of God.
1.5: For our Gospel did not come to you in word only, but in power also and in the Holy Ghost and much certainty ( as you know how we behaved among you for your sakes ).
1.6: And you became followers of us and of the Lord and received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Ghost,
1.7: so that you were examples to all believers in Macedonia and in Achaia.
1.8: For the word of the Lord has resounded from you - not only in Macedonia and in Achaia - but in all quarters. Your faith toward God has gone out, so that we need not say anything.
1.9: For they themselves tell of how we approached you and how you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God,
1.10: and to look for His Son from Heaven - Whom He raised from the dead – Who is Jesus; Who delivers us from the wrath to come.

2.1: For you yourselves know, brothers, that our coming to you was not in vain.
2.2: But even after we had suffered before ( and were insulted at Philippi, as you know ) we were emboldened by God to speak the Gospel of God to you with much struggle.
2.3: For our encouragement was not in error, nor of impurity, nor by deceit.
2.4: But just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the Gospel, so we speak - not as those who please men, but God, Who examines our hearts.
2.5: Nor did we ever at any time use flattering words ( as you know ), nor cloaked covetousness. God is our witness.
2.6: Nor did we seek the praise of men - either by you or by others - when we might have imposed on you as the Apostles of Christ.
2.7: But we were gentle among you, even as a nurse cherishes her children.
2.8: Having this affection toward you, it was our pleasure to have shared with you not only the Gospel of God, but also our own souls, because you were dear to us.
2.9: For you remember, brothers, our labor and travail. For we labored day and night ( so that we would not be a burden to any of you ) and preached to you the Gospel of God.
2.10: You and God are witnesses of how holily, and justly, and unblameably we behaved among you who believe.
2.11: As you know how we exhorted and comforted and testified to every one of you ( as a father to his children. )
2.12: So that you would walk worthy of God, Who has called you to His kingdom, and glory.
2.13: For this reason also, we thank God unceasingly that when you received the word of God ( which you heard from us ) you did not receive it as the word of men, but as it really is - the word of God - which also works in you who believe.
2.14: For brothers, you have become followers of the churches of God ( which in Judea are in Christ Jesus ) because you have also suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they have from the Judeans,
2.15: who both killed the Lord Jesus and their own Prophets and have driven us out. And they do not please God and are contrary to all men
2.16: and forbid us to preach to the Gentiles ( so that they might be saved ), always fulfilling their sins. But wrath has come upon them to the utmost.
2.17: But since, brothers, we were kept from you for a season ( as far as sight, but not in the heart ), we were eager to see your face with great desire.
2.18: Therefore, we would have come to you ( I Paul, at least once or twice ) but Satan hindered us.
2.19: For what is our hope or joy or crown of rejoicing? Is it not even you, in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at His coming?
2.20: Yes! You are our glory and joy!

3.1: Therefore, since we could endure it no longer, we thought it good to remain at Athens alone;
3.2: and have sent Timothy, our brother and minister of God and our fellow laborer in the Gospel of Christ, to establish you and to comfort you regarding your faith;
3.3: so that no one would be disturbed by these afflictions. For you yourselves know that we are appointed to this.
3.4: For truly we told you before ( when we were with you ) that we would suffer tribulations even as it happened. And you know it.
3.5: For this reason, when I could no longer bear it, I sent him. So that I might know of your faith, lest the tempter had tempted you in any way and that our labor had been in vain.
3.6: But now, lately, when Timothy came from you to us and brought us good tidings of your faith and love ( and that you have good remembrance of us always, desiring to see us, as we also you ),
3.7: therefore brothers, in all our affliction and necessity, we were encouraged by you through your faith.
3.8: For now if you stand fast in the Lord, we are alive!
3.9: For what thanks can we render to God for you - for all the joy with which we rejoice for your sakes before our God,
3.10: night and day, praying exceedingly – so that we might see your face and accomplish that which is lacking in your faith?
3.11: Now may God himself - even our Father - and our Lord Jesus Christ, guide our journey to you.
3.12: And the Lord increase you and make you abound in love toward one another, and toward all, even as we do toward you;
3.13: to make your hearts stable and unblameable in holiness before God, and our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all His saints.

4.1: Furthermore, we urge and exhort you in the Lord Jesus, brothers, that you increase more and more in how you ought to walk and to please God ( as you have received from us ).
4.2: For you know what commandments we gave you by the Lord Jesus.
4.3: For this is the will of God: your sanctification. And that you should abstain from fornication;
4.4: so that every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in holiness and honor,
4.5: not in the passion of lust ( as the Gentiles do, who do not know God ),
4.6: so that no one oppresses or defrauds his brother in any matter. For the Lord is Avenger of all such things, as we also have told you previously, and testified.
4.7: For God has not called us to uncleanness, but to holiness.
4.8: Therefore, the one who ignores these things, does not ignore man, but God ( Who has also given His Holy Spirit ).
4.9: But concerning brotherly love, you do not need me to write to you. For you are taught by God to love one another.
4.10: And, indeed, you do so to all the brothers throughout all Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to increase more and more
4.11: and to earnestly endeavor to be quiet and mind your own business; and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you;
4.12: so that you may behave honorably toward those who are outside, and that you lack nothing.
4.13: Brothers, I would not have you be ignorant concerning those who are asleep, lest you mourn as others who have no hope.
4.14: For if we believe that Jesus is dead and is risen, so also will God bring with Him those who sleep in Jesus.
4.15: For we say this to you by the word of the Lord: that we who live - and remain until the coming of the Lord - shall not precede those who sleep.
4.16: For the Lord Himself shall descend from Heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of God. And the dead in Christ shall rise first.
4.17: Then shall we who live and remain be caught up with them also in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air. And so shall we ever be with the Lord.
4.18: Therefore, comfort one another with these words.

5.1: But of the times and seasons, brothers, you have no need for me to write to you.
5.2: For you yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord shall come as a thief in the night.
5.3: For when they shall say “Peace and safety”, then sudden destruction shall come upon them, as labor upon a woman with child. And they shall not escape.
5.4: But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that that day shall come on you as a thief.
5.5: You are all children of light, and children of the day. We are not of the night, nor of darkness.
5.6: Therefore let us not sleep as others do. But, let us watch and be sober.
5.7: For those who sleep, sleep in the night. And those who are drunk, are drunk in the night.
5.8: But let us who are of the day be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love and the hope of salvation for a helmet.
5.9: For God has not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by means of our Lord Jesus Christ;
5.10: Who died for us so that - whether we wake or sleep - we would live together with Him.
5.11: Therefore, exhort one another. And edify one another, just as you are doing.
5.12: Now, we urge you, brothers, that you acknowledge those who labor among you and are over you in the Lord and admonish you.
5.13: Hold them in singular love for their work’s sake. Be at peace among yourselves.
5.14: We desire, brothers, that you admonish those who are out of order, comfort the faint - hearted, bear with the weak, be patient toward all.
5.15: See that no one recompenses evil for evil to anyone. But always follow that which is good, both toward yourselves and toward all.
5.18: Give thanks in all things. For this is the will of God toward you in Christ Jesus.
5.21: Test all things. Keep that which is good.
5.22: Abstain from any appearance of evil.
5.23: Now, may the very God of Peace sanctify you completely. And may your whole spirit and soul and body be kept blameless, until the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
5.24: Faithful is He Who calls you. He will also do it.
5.26: Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
5.27: I charge you in the Lord that this epistle be read to all the holy brothers.
5.28: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you, Amen. ( The first Epistle to the Thessalonians, written from Athens. )

1.1: Paul and Silvanus, and Timothy, To the Church of the Thessalonians, which is in God our Father, and in the Lord Jesus Christ:
1.2: Grace be with you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: We ought to thank God always for you, brothers ( as is fitting ), because your faith grows exceedingly, and the love of every one of you toward each other abounds.
1.4: So that we ourselves rejoice over you in the churches of God because of your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that you suffer.
1.5: ( a sign of the righteous judgment of God, that you may be counted worthy of the Kingdom of God, for which you also suffer ).
1.6: For it is a righteous thing with God to repay those who trouble you with tribulation.
1.7: And to you who are troubled: rest with us when the Lord Jesus shall show Himself from Heaven with His mighty angels
1.8: in flaming fire, rendering vengeance on those who do not know God and who do not obey the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ;
1.9: who shall be punished with everlasting perdition from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His power
1.10: when He shall, on that Day, come to be glorified in His saints and made marvelous in all those who believe, because our testimony toward you was believed.
1.11: Therefore, we pray always for you that our God may make you worthy of this calling and fulfill all the good pleasure of His goodness, and the work of faith, with power;
